question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To play second fiddle

options.text: To play a musical instrument badly

explanation: Play second fiddle = गौण भूमिका निभाना। Example: She refused to play second fiddle to her junior colleague.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To pass the buck

options.text: To shift responsibility to someone else

explanation: Pass the buck = ज़िम्मेदारी दूसरे पर डाल देना। Example: The manager passed the buck to his assistant.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To bell the cat

options.text: To undertake a risky task for the common good

explanation: Bell the cat = सबके हित में जोखिम भरा काम अपने ऊपर लेना। Example: Nobody dared to bell the cat and complain to the angry chief.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To smell a rat

options.text: To suspect that something is wrong

explanation: Smell a rat = कुछ गड़बड़ होने का शक होना। Example: The police smelt a rat when the shopkeeper changed his story.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To show the white feather
explanation: Show the white feather = कायरता दिखाना। Example: The soldier showed the white feather and ran away from the battle.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To toe the line

options.text: To obey rules or conform to a standard

explanation: Toe the line = नियमों का पालन करना। Example: New employees are expected to toe the line.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To fall flat

options.text: To fail to produce the intended effect

explanation: Fall flat = अपेक्षित प्रभाव न डाल पाना / फुस्स हो जाना। Example: His joke fell flat and nobody laughed.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A bone of contention
explanation: A bone of contention = झगड़े की जड़। Example: The land became a bone of contention between the two brothers.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A necessary evil
explanation: A necessary evil = अप्रिय पर अनिवार्य चीज़। Example: Many people consider taxes a necessary evil.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To burn one's boats

options.text: To cut off all means of retreat

explanation: Burn one's boats = वापसी के सारे रास्ते बंद कर देना। Example: By resigning without another job, he burnt his boats.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To add fuel to the fire

options.text: To make a bad situation worse

explanation: Add fuel to the fire = आग में घी डालना। Example: His angry reply only added fuel to the fire.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To rest on one's oars

options.text: To relax after a period of effort

explanation: Rest on one's oars = मेहनत के बाद आराम करना / ढीले पड़ जाना। Example: Having topped the exam once, he should not rest on his oars.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To read between the lines
explanation: Read between the lines = छिपा हुआ अर्थ समझना। Example: If you read between the lines, the letter is actually a warning.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To turn a deaf ear
explanation: Turn a deaf ear = अनसुना कर देना। Example: The officer turned a deaf ear to the villagers' complaints.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To run amok

options.text: To behave in a wild, uncontrollable manner

explanation: Run amok = उन्मत्त होकर उत्पात मचाना। Example: The angry crowd ran amok and damaged the shops.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To take the wind out of one's sails

options.text: To cool down a hot argument
To deflate someone by destroying his confidence

explanation: Take the wind out of one's sails = किसी का उत्साह/आत्मविश्वास ठंडा कर देना। Example: The sudden defeat took the wind out of the team's sails.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To steal a march on

options.text: To gain an advantage by acting earlier than others

explanation: Steal a march on = चुपके से दूसरों से आगे निकल जाना। Example: The company stole a march on its rivals by launching the product early.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To sail close to the wind

options.text: To take a risk by almost breaking rules

explanation: Sail close to the wind = नियमों की सीमा पर जोखिम भरा काम करना। Example: The accountant was sailing close to the wind with those figures.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To pour oil on troubled waters
explanation: Pour oil on troubled waters = झगड़ा शांत करना। Example: The elder poured oil on troubled waters and ended the dispute.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To throw dust in the eyes
explanation: Throw dust in the eyes = आँखों में धूल झोंकना, धोखा देना। Example: The agent tried to throw dust in our eyes with false documents.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To eat one's words

options.text: To retract what one has said

explanation: Eat one's words = अपनी कही बात वापस लेना। Example: He had to eat his words when the project succeeded.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To keep the wolf from the door

options.text: To guard a house from animals

explanation: Keep the wolf from the door = भुखमरी/गरीबी से बचे रहना। Example: His small salary barely kept the wolf from the door.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To have an axe to grind
explanation: Have an axe to grind = अपना स्वार्थ साधना। Example: Don't trust his advice; he has an axe to grind.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A feather in one's cap

options.text: An achievement to be proud of

explanation: A feather in one's cap = गौरव की बात / उपलब्धि। Example: The gold medal was a feather in her cap.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To hold out the olive branch
explanation: Hold out the olive branch = सुलह का प्रस्ताव देना। Example: The company held out the olive branch to the striking workers.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A red herring

options.text: A misleading clue that diverts attention

explanation: A red herring = ध्यान भटकाने वाला झूठा सुराग। Example: The detective realised the stolen purse was a red herring.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: Achilles' heel
explanation: Achilles' heel = कमज़ोर पक्ष / दुखती रग। Example: Lack of money was the Achilles' heel of his plan.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To keep at bay
explanation: Keep at bay = दूर रखना / पास न आने देना। Example: A good diet helps to keep illness at bay.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To split hairs
explanation: Split hairs = बाल की खाल निकालना। Example: Let us not split hairs over a small difference.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To take the cake

options.text: To be the best or the most outrageous

explanation: Take the cake = सबसे बढ़कर निकलना (अक्सर बुरे अर्थ में)। Example: His excuse for being late really takes the cake.
